key_insight: Linking fracture-tip sampling distance to mesh resolution enables convergent stress intensity factor estimates where conventional nearest-tip sampling fails.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stress intensity factors support accurate predictions of whether pre-existing fractures will propagate.
method: Extract stress intensity factors using two-point displacement correlation.
Balance asymptotic truncation error against numerical discretization error to derive a sampling-distance scaling law.
Validate with quadratic finite elements, quarter-point finite elements, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method.
evidence_signal: Pure-mode and mixed-mode fracture benchmarks showed decreasing stress intensity factor errors under mesh refinement with scaling-based sampling across all three discretization methods.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the scaling formula or implementation constants; these must be checked before applying the method.
paper_title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
